fallback: I can only answer questions about Indian GST. Please rephrase your question.

answers.what is gst?: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is a destination-based indirect tax on the supply of goods and services in India. It replaced most central and state indirect taxes on 1 July 2017.
answers.what is the difference between cgst, sgs: On a supply within one state (intra-state), GST is split equally into CGST, collected by the Centre, and SGST or UTGST, collected by the state or union territory. On a supply between states (inter-state), or on an import, the full rate is charged as IGST, collected by the Centre.
answers.when is gst registration mandatory?: Registration is mandatory once aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds Rs 40 lakh for suppliers of goods only, or Rs 20 lakh for suppliers of services (Rs 20 lakh and Rs 10 lakh in special category states). Some suppliers must register whatever their turnover, for example inter-state suppliers of taxable goods, e-commerce operators and persons liable to pay tax under reverse charge.
answers.what is a gstin?: A GSTIN is the 15-character GST identification number. The first 2 digits are the state code, the next 10 characters are the PAN of the business, the 13th is the entity number for that PAN in the state, the 14th is 'Z' by default and the 15th is a check character.
answers.what is input tax credit?: Input tax credit (ITC) lets a registered person reduce the GST payable on their sales by the GST already paid on purchases used in the course of business. Conditions apply: a valid tax invoice, the supplier must have reported the invoice, and the goods or services must have been received.
answers.what is the composition scheme?: The composition scheme lets small taxpayers pay GST at a fixed percentage of turnover with simpler compliance. It is available when aggregate turnover in the previous financial year is up to Rs 1.5 crore (Rs 75 lakh in special category states), or up to Rs 50 lakh for most service providers. Composition taxpayers cannot collect GST from customers or claim input tax credit.
answers.what is reverse charge?: Under reverse charge the recipient of a supply pays the GST to the government instead of the supplier. It applies to notified goods and services, such as goods transport agency services or legal services from an advocate to a business, and to certain supplies from unregistered persons.
answers.when is gstr-1 due?: Monthly filers must file GSTR-1 (details of outward supplies) by the 11th of the following month. Taxpayers in the QRMP scheme file it quarterly, by the 13th of the month after the quarter.
answers.when is gstr-3b due?: Monthly filers must file GSTR-3B (summary return with tax payment) by the 20th of the following month. Quarterly filers in the QRMP scheme file by the 22nd or 24th of the month after the quarter, depending on their state.
answers.what is an e-way bill?: An e-way bill is an electronic document needed to move goods worth more than Rs 50,000 in one consignment. It is generated on the e-way bill portal before the movement starts. Some states set a different threshold for movement within the state.
answers.what is e-invoicing?: E-invoicing means reporting B2B invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal, which returns an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a signed QR code. It is mandatory for businesses whose aggregate turnover exceeded Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards.
answers.what is an hsn code?: HSN (Harmonised System of Nomenclature) codes classify goods for GST. Tax invoices must show 4 digits if aggregate turnover in the previous year was up to Rs 5 crore, and 6 digits above that. Services use SAC (Services Accounting Code) instead.
answers.what is place of supply?: The place of supply decides whether a transaction is intra-state (CGST + SGST) or inter-state (IGST). For goods it is generally where the movement of the goods ends. For services it is generally the location of a registered recipient, with specific rules for services such as immovable property, events and transport.
answers.what are the gst rates?: Since 22 September 2025 most goods and services fall into two main slabs, 5% and 18%, with a 40% rate for a small set of luxury and sin goods. Some items are exempt, and special rates apply to items such as gold.
answers.what is the gst rate on restaurant servi: Restaurant services are taxed at 5% without input tax credit. Restaurants inside hotels where any room is priced above Rs 7,500 per day are taxed at 18% with input tax credit.
answers.what is the interest on late gst payment: Interest on late payment of GST is 18% per year on the tax paid in cash, counted from the day after the due date until the date of payment.
answers.what is the late fee for gstr-3b?: The late fee for GSTR-3B is Rs 50 per day (Rs 25 CGST + Rs 25 SGST), or Rs 20 per day for a nil return, subject to caps that depend on turnover.
